problem.name_latex: Identity and uniformity testing of finite distributions
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Uniformity testing of a finite distribution.} Given coherent access to a classical sampler for $p$ on $[N]$, distinguish $p=u_N$ from $\|p-u_N\|_1\ge\varepsilon$, where $u_N(i)=1/N$. Classical access uses ordinary independent samples.

\textbf{Identity testing of a finite distribution.} Given a known distribution $q$ on $[N]$ and coherent sampler access to $p$, distinguish $p=q$ from $\|p-q\|_1\ge\varepsilon$. The known probabilities of $q$ can be evaluated as required by the reduction.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Uniformity testing of a finite distribution.} $O(N^{1/3}/\varepsilon^2)$ coherent sampler queries by Bravyi--Harrow--Hassidim and Chakraborty--Fischer--Matsliah--de Wolf; the $N^{1/3}$ dependence is optimal at constant distance.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Identity testing of a finite distribution.} $O(N^{1/3}\log^2N\log\log N/\varepsilon^5)$ queries by Chakraborty--Fischer--Matsliah--de Wolf via reduction to uniformity testing.
quantum.headline_text: Uniformity testing of a finite distribution. $O(N^{1/3}/\varepsilon^2)$ coherent sampler queries by Bravyi–Harrow–Hassidim and Chakraborty–Fischer–Matsliah–de Wolf; the $N^{1/3}$ dependence is optimal at constant distance.
quantum.details_text: Identity testing of a finite distribution. $O(N^{1/3}\log^2N\log\log N/\varepsilon^5)$ queries by Chakraborty–Fischer–Matsliah–de Wolf via reduction to uniformity testing.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Uniformity testing of a finite distribution.} $\Theta(\sqrt N/\varepsilon^2)$ samples by collision or chi-square uniformity testers in the standard nondegenerate range.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Identity testing of a finite distribution.} $\Theta(\sqrt N/\varepsilon^2)$ samples in the worst case over known reference distributions, with sharper instance-dependent bounds for a specified $q$.
